set.n: $1,300 in gold plowed up, old Patrick Callahan farm (found 1921)
set.tovw: Recovered 1921; AP original read; $19,300 figure was a relay error
set.st: In May 1921 farm hand John Brazell (Brassell) plowed up a glass fruit jar of gold coins, $2.50 to $20 pieces, about $1,300 in all, in a field on the old Patrick Callahan farm near Lansing; it had been buried for many years. One wire copy printed $19,300; the Iowa copies say $1,300. Recovered May 1921; nothing more reported. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.

src: Davenport Daily Times, 3 May 1921, p. 1 'Finds $1,300 in Gold Buried on Iowa Farm' (Newspapers.com 301698625; same AP wire Quad-City Times, Waterloo Courier, Cedar Rapids Gazette)

set.n: Jar of gold under the old barn sill, Schultz farm SW of Deerfield (found 1920)
set.pl: 15-acre farm SW of Deerfield (former Edward Meyer land); not placed on the 1907 plat; pin on GNIS Deerfield
set.st: Sept 1920: moving an old barn on his 15-acre farm SW of Deerfield (bought from Edward Meyer), Adolph Schultz and neighbour boy Raymond Horenberger found a glass jar with $1,800 in gold coins (dated about 1850) and currency under the sill. Recovered Sept 1920; the whole-place digging was the owner's follow-up, nothing more reported. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.

src: Libertyville Independent, 2 Sep 1920, p. 1 'Mystery Surrounds Finding $1800 Gold in Deerfield Barn' (Newspapers.com 699394965)

set.pl: Wethersfield Twp, 4 mi directly S of Kewanee (Kewanee Star 1897); farm not yet on a plat
set.tovw: Hoard rumour; robbers found no money 1897
set.st: Aug 9 1897: two robbers bound, gagged, clubbed and tortured James Johnston, about 60, a Wethersfield Twp farmer living alone four miles directly south of Kewanee in a rambling old house screened by cottonwoods, evergreens, box elders and a hedge. He was reported to have hoarded his wealth in a 'treasure box'; they got about $1 and a gold watch, and 'there was no money in the house'. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.

src: Kewanee Star, 12 Aug 1897, p. 1 'Attempted Robbery / James Johnston Bound and Gagged' (Newspapers.com 755758978; Rock Island Argus 13 Aug same wire)

set.tovw: Two papers; hidden recess sworn to; no recovery
set.t: Private farm (now suburban); no recovery reported; recess not located.

tw-il-northbrook-tatge-1924.st: Ferdinand Tatge, 58, a hermit farmer, was found shot in a locked corn crib; he was rumoured to keep money in an old tin pail, and banker Adolph Lauer testified that Tatge would bring a gallon pail from a hidden recess and dump greenbacks on a table.
src: Chicago Tribune, 12 Jan 1924, p. 1 'Slain for Hoard, Theory' (Newspapers.com 354902321)

set.tovw: Recovered 1934; UP original read; mill razed
set.st: March 1934: CCC worker Stanley Wojtysiak, razing the 100-year-old Kammeyer grist mill at Fullersburg, chopped into a brick wall and a tin box of old $10 and $20 bills (about $4,200) fell out. When the former operator Kammeyer died, relatives from Rome, N.Y. had searched in vain for his $4,000+ savings. Recovered March 1934; the mill was razed; nothing more reported. The surviving Graue Mill at Fullersburg is a different mill.

src: Belleville News-Democrat, 20 Mar 1934, p. 3 'CCC Man Finds Cache of $4200 in Old Grist Mill' (Newspapers.com 769026511; Urbana Courier 19 Mar p. 2, 898600743, same UP wire)

set.tovw: One 1964 item; police believed children took it
set.st: April 1964: two men admitted burgling $500 in coins from a Rochelle grocery and said they hid them in a pillowcase under a railroad bridge in town; police never found the coins. The burglars were two Rochelle men, 23 and 22; police thought children may have taken the coins. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.

src: Dixon Evening Telegraph, 21 Apr 1964, p. 4 'Rochelle Men Held' (Newspapers.com 86120807)
